measure: COREX vs conventional BF: fuel savings
note: Reported for a low-export-gas system demonstration in India; oxygen consumption -13%, slag -18%, NOx about -30% per t product. reprinted from APP 2010; Siemens VAI 2007 [8,34]

measure: FINEX vs BF: capital and production cost
note: 'Capital cost claimed to be 20 percent lower than for BF, and production cost 15 percent lower' (the source labels this list 'benefits ... for COREX'). reprinted from APP 2010; Siemens VAI 2007 [8,34]
Also 10% savings over an EAF fed by DRI (Mesabi Nugget claim). reprinted from Mesabi Nugget 2011 [29]

measure: Paired straight hearth furnace vs BF ironmaking
note: '30 percent less energy at lower capital cost compared to BF ironmaking'. reprinted from APP 2010; U.S. DOE/ITP 2011 [8,40]
Any of the three reductants; savings mainly from eliminating coke making, pelletizing and sintering. reprinted from AISI 2010 [7]

measure: Hydrogen flash smelting vs BF (earlier Univ. of Utah study)
note: 'more than 50 percent of conventional BF energy use'. reprinted from AISI 2010 [7]
Computational model predicts RHF productivity gains up to 50% from replacing coal with wood charcoal; not an energy saving. reprinted from Fruehan 2004b [23]
